content.text: {"label":"outage","explanation":"A P2 incident on the IMPS/NEFT payment hub (opened 12:30) reports outward transfers stuck as pending: accounts are debited but credits are not confirmed, and a reversal job is queued. Payments volume jumped from about +5% to +40–53% over forecast starting at 12:15. All of the excess comes from payment_status_enquiry (1.6x normal, +67 calls) and refund_status (1.66x, +56.6 calls), which are exactly the reasons a stuck-transfer incident would drive. Other payment reasons are at or below normal. Payments staffing is on plan (36 on phones vs 36 planned) and attendance is normal, so this is not a supply problem. Payments AHT rose to 356 s, consistent with harder outage calls. General is near forecast at 84% service level. The KYC SMS and the P4 internal incidents do not match the pattern.","plan_name":"IMPS outage: deflect status calls, add payments capacity","rationale":"Payments is carrying roughly 60 Erlangs of workload against 36 agents. Demand levers come first because they are free or cheap. A known-issue IVR message on the two rising reasons should stop about 20% of those callers, and 20% chat deflection on the same reasons removes more at Rs 12 per chat. On the supply side, coaching is cancelled and pre-14:00 breaks are delayed 45 min to cover the immediate backlog until overtime arrives. Overtime is offered in two consecutive 2-hour blocks, starting 13:15 because of the 30-minute lead time. Expected acceptance is about 8 and 6 agents, roughly Rs 10,000, within the Rs 15,000 budget. Only 3 agents move from general: it runs about 28 Erlangs on 34 agents at 84% service level, so a larger move would push it below the 70% donor floor.
